details:
TropicMap: From Space Data to Early Action

TropicMap is a satellite-based early-warning project concept designed to identify areas that may experience agricultural stress before its effects become clearly visible.

How It Works:

The proposed system combines four environmental indicators derived from satellite observations:

  • Vegetation Health (NDVI/EVI)
  • Land Surface Temperature (LST)
  • Precipitation (GPM IMERG)
  • Soil Moisture (SMAP L4)

These indicators are intended to be compared with historical or regional environmental conditions to identify unusual patterns that may indicate agricultural stress. The results would be presented through a simple early-warning map highlighting areas that may require further investigation.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

TropicMap aims to support earlier awareness of agricultural stress, help farmers make better-informed decisions, improve crop monitoring, and encourage more efficient water resource management. By combining different environmental observations, the project seeks to make satellite information easier to understand and more useful for agricultural decision-making.

Tools and Data Sources:

The project identifies NASA Earth observation datasets, including MODIS MOD13Q1, MODIS MOD11A2, GPM IMERG, and SMAP L4, as planned data sources for future integration. The current submission presents the project concept and proposed workflow; these datasets have not yet been processed as part of an operational system.

Canva was used to prepare the project presentation, and ChatGPT was used to assist with writing and organizing project content. No operational software, custom code, or hardware implementation is claimed in the current version.

Creativity and Innovation:

The main creative aspect of TropicMap is its approach of combining four complementary environmental indicators into one agricultural early-warning concept. Instead of considering vegetation, temperature, rainfall, and soil moisture separately, the project proposes bringing them together to provide a broader picture of environmental conditions.

Factors Considered:

The project considers the importance of early detection, the availability of satellite observations, differences between environmental indicators, and the need to compare results with real agricultural observations. It also recognizes that satellite-based indicators cannot replace field inspections or professional agricultural advice.

Future Development:

Future improvements include integrating and processing the planned NASA datasets, developing an interactive mapping platform, testing the approach in different agricultural regions, and improving the accuracy of potential risk identification and alerts.
